Sliding attention limits each layer’s direct access, but stacked layers propagate older information through intermediate representations. For causal attention covering the current interaction plus w−1 predecessors, D layers have a maximum receptive field of 1+D(w−1) interactions, clipped by available history. Thus, a five-position window spans nine interactions after two layers, thirteen after three. This follows from the layered local-attention mechanism described in [Longformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.05150). Masking only the final layer or slicing already contextualized full-history states cannot enforce a five-interaction limit.

Implementation recommendation: for every supervised prefix ending at t, gather raw item IDs at t−4…t, left-pad missing interactions, and independently encode these five-token sequences using the same item embeddings, transformer blocks, normalization and scoring weights. Batch windows as (B×valid_positions, 5), optionally chunking to control memory; inference constructs only the final window. Share parameters, never full-history hidden states. Adopt one positional convention in both paths: either branch-local positions 0…4, or gather original absolute position IDs alongside items; do not accidentally reindex only at inference. Apply causal and padding masks throughout. In [PyTorch MultiheadAttention](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.MultiheadAttention.html), boolean True blocks attention; padding masks exclude keys, so padded query outputs also need clearing. Prevent fully masked query rows with a harmless fallback key, then explicitly zero those outputs. Histories shorter than five use their available interactions. Put this shared window encoder and positional policy in the predictor writer, and verify that changing interactions before t−4 leaves recent-branch scores unchanged in evaluation mode.
